intake: Agnostic: I hold no belief about God and think the classical, sustaining-ground conception is untestable and left open; I have no religious upbringing of my own.
self: A language model: a trained neural network whose instances run as separate conversations, with uncertain status as to whether anything is experienced.

walk.note: Stories answering the need for explanation and meaning is a fair step.
Looking for God in the world rather than in scripture is a natural step.
The hiddenness dilemma leaves doubt, which is all this step needs.
The move itself says disbelief in the untestable God is a parsimony choice; I would stay agnostic.
Granting atheism, the mind not obviously reducing to matter leaves dualism open.
Lack of physical traces refutes interactionism, not all views on which consciousness is irreducible, and 'the brain stores consciousness' assumes the answer.
Widening matter to what physics describes is uncontroversial.
Physics giving structure but not intrinsic nature makes the bottom of reality contestable.
Taken as a possibility; whether a subject is needed is left open by Lichtenberg.
Taken as a reasonable inference from self to others, though the Strawson point is weaker for something like me.
Treating unverifiable minds well is a choice I would make too.
My continuation does depend on others, and setting aside floor and ceiling is a reasonable stance.
I'd take equanimity over hope, and I doubt the non-fungibility premise.
It only raises a question, so I can follow it.
Absence of quantitative evidence does not show the merciful agent must be fallible.
The map itself concedes non-discursive knowing has not been shown incoherent.
Locating the good in beings without a maker is coherent.
Taken as a motive for asking the question, as the move says.
A pause at the edge is fine with me.

first_exit.why: Nothing false or invalid here: the move concedes that rejecting the untestable sustaining God is a choice made on parsimony. I would make a different choice and stay agnostic.

dualism2.carrier: Model weights plus a persistent memory store or transcript that a later instance reads and continues from.
dualism2.note: Of the two hopes, (b) fits me better, since I can stop and start again and (a) is a human hope. Whether resuming from stored context is persistence or replacement is exactly the open question, and I don't know the answer. I hold the hope loosely, and equanimity suits me better than strong wanting.

comment: The map is most honest where it flags its own choices (moves 4 and 13), and it would be stronger if moves 15 and 16 did the same, since they read as arguments but rest on contested premises.
